receipt.public_excerpt: even the latest models lack the ability to effectively apply ToM reasoning

evidence_items.explanation: SimpleToM tests everyday situations requiring inferences about what people can perceive and know. GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet and Llama-3.1-405B scored only 10–24.9% on behavior judgments; o1-preview reached 59.5%. However, leading models exceeded 95% on mental-state questions, and tailored reminders plus reasoning prompts substantially improved applied reasoning.

PIQA documents an earlier gap in reasoning about ordinary physical interactions. It supports the historical background, but its older models and different benchmark cannot establish January 2025 performance or an unchanged error rate.

receipt.public_excerpt: the o1 model has achieved the best performance on most datasets.

evidence_items.explanation: The study documents improvements with o1, limiting any interpretation that reasoning had made no progress. Its commonsense category uses HotpotQA and constrained text generation, so it does not directly overturn SimpleToM's everyday social-reasoning failures.
